items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Lionel Hampton came, kissed the bride and jammed for hours!

ctx.x: Bernard Peiffer had a very personal style, and sometimes, he could do a good imitation of Erroll Garner. But when he got excited his taste was bad and he seemed to be giving instructions on how to break a piano up in public without using an ax.

Michel de Villers had learned a lot from Charlie Parker records, and played the style well. His only draw back was that he didn't read music. Geo Daly was considered the Lionel Hampton of France. He and Peiffer did a Hamp and Milt Buckner act on the piano with Geo (pronounced Gee-o) doing the one finger bit like Hamp, and that always pleased the audiance. Jean Bouchety was a fine bass fiddle man, arranger and pilot. But I never knew if he had flown a plane during the war. Roger Paraboschi played solid drums which…

Eventually, I ran into "Big Boy" Goddie, who had spent the 2nd world war years in South America. I also later saw Arthur Briggs, who had been in a concentration camp after the Germans occupied Paris. Briggs told me why the few of the old gang that was still in Parid did not hang around in Boudon's anymore. The owner had collaborated with the Germans, and had denounced some Jews and Negros. I had been eating in the place, but went somewhere else after hearing what Briggs told me.
